<!-- Generated by dev-env -->

This is the maintenance skill: it turns "bring this repo up to standard" into a concrete,
repeatable procedure instead of an ad hoc guess.

## Procedure

1. **Read every contract.** For each `.agents/skills/*/SKILL.md` that has a `## Contract`
   section, read it. Every bullet under `## Contract` is a statement that must be true of
   this repo right now — not a suggestion, not a future goal.
2. **Audit against each bullet**, and fix any deviation using the guidance already
   written in that skill's own body — don't reinvent the fix. Two things stay off-limits
   while fixing:
   - Any file whose content begins with the line `<!-- Generated by dev-env -->`. It is
     rewritten byte-for-byte on the next `dev-env apply`; a hand-edit is drift that gets
     silently reverted. If the generated shape is genuinely wrong, that's a dev-env bug —
     report it upstream — not something to patch locally.
   - Any other file a skill explicitly names as dev-env–owned in its contract bullet.
3. **Verify inside the devcontainer** — never on the host:
   `devcontainer exec --workspace-folder . pnpm lint`,
   `devcontainer exec --workspace-folder . pnpm typecheck`,
   `devcontainer exec --workspace-folder . pnpm test:run`.
4. **Open a PR** titled `Converge on dev-env standards`, with a description listing each
   contract item that was out of compliance and how it was resolved. Split unrelated
   items into separate commits where practical — one commit per unrelated item — so the
   PR stays reviewable and any one item can be reverted without the others.

## What `AGENTS.md` must contain

`AGENTS.md` is loaded on every session, so it holds only what nearly every change needs —
nothing that is merely useful sometimes:

- **Command routing.** Toolchain commands — `pnpm`, `npx`, `node`, and any build, test,
  lint, or typecheck — run inside the devcontainer: `devcontainer exec
--workspace-folder . <command>`, never directly on the host. `git` and `gh` run on the
  host, never in the container. `devcontainer up --workspace-folder .` starts the
  container. A Cursor cloud agent VM is **not** the devcontainer and inverts that first
  rule — load the `dev-environment` skill before running anything there.
- **The project's own always-needed context** — what the app is, how it's shaped — kept
  short.
- **A Skills index table**: one row per skill, naming it and the one-line trigger for
  when to load it.

Anything needed only sometimes belongs in a skill, not in `AGENTS.md`. If `AGENTS.md`
carries a long section that reads as a skill — a subsystem's design, a multi-step
workflow, a checklist for a recurring task — move it to
`.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` with a trigger-style `description` and leave a single
row behind in the index.

`CLAUDE.md` must begin with `@AGENTS.md`, with nothing else duplicated below it — Claude
Code loads `AGENTS.md` through that import, so a second copy of its content just goes
stale.

`.cursor/rules/*.mdc` files should not exist. Cursor reads `AGENTS.md` natively; a
`.mdc` file is a second instruction source that inevitably drifts from it. Delete any
that are found rather than keeping them in sync by hand.

## Contract

- `AGENTS.md` holds only command routing, the project's own always-needed context, and a
  skills index — everything sometimes-needed lives in a skill instead.
- `CLAUDE.md`'s first line is `@AGENTS.md`.
- No `.cursor/rules/*.mdc` files exist.
